lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with Anchorage businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Anchorage is Alaska's commercial hub: the place the rest of the state comes to shop, see a specialist, catch a flight or hire a contractor. We plan marketing for the customers that brings you, from neighbours in South Anchorage to a family flying in from a village for a week of appointments and errands.

sections.heading: The city the state runs through
paragraphs: Most of Alaska's business passes through Anchorage in some way. Oil and gas companies keep their offices here, Alaska Native corporations have headquarters or major operations in the city, and Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport is among the world's busiest air cargo airports, a stop between Asia and North America. Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson adds a large military community that turns over regularly as families are posted in and out.

Healthcare is another pillar. The hospitals and clinics of the U-Med District, including Providence and the Alaska Native Medical Center, treat patients from all over the state. The same is true of retail: people from the Kenai, the Valley and communities off the road system make trips to Anchorage to stock up.
So an Anchorage business often has two markets, the people who live here and the people who come in on purpose. Both look you up before they arrive.

sections.heading: How Anchorage is laid out
paragraphs: Downtown holds the hotels, the visitor trade and offices. Midtown is the business core, with banks, corporate buildings and restaurants. Spenard has independent shops, bars and music venues. South Anchorage, around Dimond Boulevard and Huffman, is where much of the big retail and newer housing sits, and the Hillside climbs toward the Chugach mountains above it. Muldoon lies to the east near the base. Eagle River and Chugiak, to the north, and Girdwood, the ski town to the south, are part of the municipality but feel like separate places.
Many customers also commute from Wasilla and Palmer. A service business needs to decide whether it covers the Valley, and say so.
bullets: Pages for the areas you serve: Midtown, South Anchorage, Eagle River, Girdwood, the Valley.
A Google Business Profile with correct winter and summer hours.
Ad targeting that includes or excludes the Mat-Su on purpose, not by default.
Clear information for out-of-town customers: parking, appointments, delivery and freight.

sections.heading: Light, dark and the dividend
paragraphs: Anchorage has a summer of long daylight and a winter of short days, and spending follows. From late spring, visitors pass through on their way to Denali, Seward and the cruise docks at Whittier, and residents put money into fishing, camping, building and home projects while the weather allows. Restaurants, tour desks, car rental and gear shops near downtown see their busiest weeks.

Winter belongs to locals. Heating repair, tyre changeovers, auto glass and remote starters are steady searches, and Fur Rendezvous and the ceremonial start of the Iditarod bring crowds downtown in late winter. In autumn, the Permanent Fund Dividend puts money in residents' accounts and almost every retailer in town runs a dividend sale. Anchorage has no sales tax, which shoppers from other communities notice.

presence: TDM works with Anchorage businesses remotely. We have no office or staff in the city. Calls are scheduled around Alaska time, and all work is delivered online by one team with written reports.

faqs.q: Does TDM have a team in Anchorage?
faqs.a: No. We work with Anchorage businesses remotely, with video calls set for Alaska time and reports you can read whenever suits you.

faqs.q: How do I reach customers in Eagle River, Wasilla and Palmer from Anchorage?
faqs.a: Decide which areas you will serve, then give each a page on your site, set the service area in your business profile and include those places in your ad targeting. Mention travel charges or minimums up front so the calls you get are ones you want.

faqs.q: What does digital marketing cost for an Anchorage business?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope of work and how competitive your trade is. We provide a quote after a free consultation.

faqs.q: Should my Anchorage business advertise all year or only in summer?
faqs.a: It depends on who buys from you. Visitor businesses should concentrate spending on the planning months and the season itself. Businesses serving residents usually do better with steady visibility and extra budget around dividend season and the first cold weeks.
